page: Amazon Web Services c6a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. It lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include an onboard GPU, comes with no local instance storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results show solid compute execution across varied workloads. The instance registers strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng with a score of 2993.35, placing it in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is solid with a stress-ng score of 23946.82, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9683.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 23583.63. Small-model LLM text generation shows high throughput at 300.58 tokens per second. Conversely, memory subsystem benchmarks reveal significant limitations when accessing large, uncached blocks. Read-only throughput on 256 MB blocks reaches 39.28 GB/sec and write throughput reaches 21.76 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the lower quartile despite a high small-block cached read speed of 1140.64 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c6a.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-cost profile using AMD EPYC silicon, serving tasks requiring sustained integer throughput and dedicated CPU cycles without the cost overhead of attached hardware accelerators or high RAM ratios. The absence of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, while the moderate memory density limits in-memory processing scales. The instance is well matched for compute-bound batch processing, Clang software compilation, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, static web serving, and mid-scale web services.
